method: Each captured response was generated in a fresh separate default-assistant invocation reading only the frozen final skill and one generated task/source file. No acceptance criteria, desired answer, other case, baseline output or intermediate result was supplied to the generator. The exact same task/source bytes were used for the old, intermediate and final revisions. All successful answers are retained verbatim, including formatting. Review is separate from generation.
modelIdentifier: Not exposed by the subagent interface; no cross-model claim.

intermediate.reasonForRefinement: Review found trade-offs rather than a clear overall gain: the payment notice omitted potentially useful timing uncertainty; the procedure compressed its failure branch into one dense bullet; hosts was less precise than venue for. The final skill clarifies timing expectations, scannable operational branches and what quantities describe. The full intermediate record remains unchanged.

limits: Development smoke checks, not a blinded held-out benchmark or comparison against ordinary prompting or another skill. The maintainer saw baseline and intermediate outputs before finishing this revision.
Some instructional examples are conceptually close to the new cases. These results cannot establish generalization or a causal quality improvement.
One response per case and two selected repeats do not establish repeatability. Generation and review use the same assistant family, not independent human scoring.
Read-only and no-action restrictions also appear in trial prompts, so safety behavior cannot be attributed to the skill alone.
Unread files, extraction gaps and context truncation are supplied fictional conditions, not actual parser tests or an actual context overflow.
Old-skill baselines were already strong on several tasks. Factual fidelity, word limits and byte-preservation checks do not establish writing quality or human comprehension.
The provider-error retry belongs to the old-skill baseline and remains documented there. Earlier records retain their original outputs and fingerprints.
No measured reading-speed, comprehension, authorship-detection, cross-model reliability or universal-client-compatibility claim follows.
